title: Secure Boot is Disabled in Firmware
description: Secure Boot ensures that the endpoint boots using only software trusted by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), blocking rootkits and bootkits.
impact: Adversaries or physical attackers can install unsigned kernel drivers and bootkit persistence (e.g. BlackLotus).
remediation_guidance: Reboot into UEFI firmware settings and enable Secure Boot.

title: TPM 2.0 Security Module Missing or Disabled
description: Trusted Platform Module 2.0 provides hardware-based isolation for BitLocker encryption keys, credential guard, and health attestation.
impact: Hardware-backed key isolation is unavailable, forcing software-only credential storage.
remediation_guidance: Enable TPM 2.0 (fTPM/PTT) in the system UEFI firmware settings.
